title: Mixed colours

brief.story: The control panel has a red power light and a blue Bluetooth light side by side, and the client wants them equally bright: both at 13–16 mA. Different colours drop different voltages, so one resistor value won’t fit both.
brief.goal: Fit a resistor for each LED so both carry 13–16 mA.

hints: Each LED has its own branch from column 3: red LEDR in columns 10–12, blue LEDB in 17–19. Each needs its own resistor from column 3.
The resistor gets 9 V minus the LED’s forward voltage: 7 V for red, but only 6 V for blue.
Red: 7 V ÷ 470 Ω = 14.9 mA. Blue: 6 V ÷ 390 Ω = 15.4 mA. 470 Ω on the blue one gives only 12.8 mA.

spec.explain: A blue LED drops 3.0 V, a red one 2.0 V: the blue one’s resistor gets 1 V less, so it needs a smaller value for the same current.

debrief: Same current, same brightness: but a blue LED keeps 3 V for itself and a red one only 2 V, so their resistors differ (470 Ω and 390 Ω here). Every multi-colour status panel and RGB LED is sized this way, one resistor per colour.
